canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Reviewer-1 assessed the epic as complete with three non-blocking observations about documented limitations. Reviewer-2 identified two major blocking findings (EV-001, EV-002) concerning Story 1 thread identity on reload and --resume operator selection. Both findings are supported by code evidence: the implementation explicitly acknowledges cwd-most-recent reload reattach as an Epic-1 convenience with concurrent same-cwd limitations (thread-resolution.ts:118-121) and most-recent auto-selection as a spec deviation due to PI's lack of interactive input (index.ts:181-190). The Story 1 verification artifact (014-verify.json) confirms both SV-001 and SV-002 are 'needs-human-ruling' with gates passing but production behavior deviating from literal AC requirements. Because Reviewer-2 returned block and the deviations are acknowledged in-code with no human-ruling accepting them, the conservative position preserves the block.
crossStoryFindings: Cross-story consistency is strong across Stories 2-6. The plain-data-only rule (AC-1.3) is consistently enforced — only SessionState is retained across hooks, no PI context objects.
Turn derivation logic is consistent throughout — turn_end events are emitted only at agent_end, ignoring PI's per-step turn_end boundaries (AC-2.2).
Idempotency key construction uses the same tiered approach (entryId → toolCallId → responseId → fallback) across capture, replay, and fork paths (AC-2.6).
Module boundaries are clean: lifecycle, capture, inference, and verify surfaces maintain separation of concerns with no internal module mocking.
architectureFindings: Implementation closely follows the tech design's module architecture. The hook rail in index.ts correctly routes to appropriate handlers.
The converter is properly decomposed into map-message (pure), turn-accumulator (state machine), idempotency (pure), and converter (orchestration) as designed.
Capture failure isolation matches the design contract: writable thread failures produce durable gaps via runtime_note events; store-unavailable failures surface as health signals (AC-2.7).
Inference routing correctly treats provider/model as opaque routing keys, with real PI model registry resolution via dynamic import.
Fork implementation follows the Epic 1 design: detection via session_before_fork hook with PI session tree fallback, seeding by event replay, source thread immutability verified (AC-3.1, AC-3.2).
The two blocking deviations are acknowledged design positions taken in Epic 1 as conveniences pending Feature 2+ permanent lineage metadata.
epicCoverageAssessment: Story 0 (Foundation): Complete — extension loads, registers Epic 1 observe-only hook rail, plain-data state holder established, fixture infrastructure in place.

Story 1 (Lifecycle): Complete with acknowledged deviations — instance init/dispose with flush, thread resolution by launch mode (new/--session/--continue), reload reconstruction uses cwd-most-recent for no-flag/--resume (SV-001 documented deviation), cwd-scoped picker with most-recent auto-selection (SV-002 documented deviation).

Story 2 (Capture): Complete — PI→LHC event mapping with content-part fan-out, turn derivation (one LHC turn per agent run), parallel tool correlation by toolCallId, error-result capture, graceful abort handling, runtime-change capture, idempotency-keyed dedup, capture-failure isolation (AC-2.1 through AC-2.8).

Story 3 (Verification): Complete — corpus replay through real converter, read-back comparison against fixtures, deterministic replay verified, inspect overview/health surfaces (AC-6.1 through AC-6.3).

Story 4 (Fork): Complete — fork detection (hook + PI session tree fallback), new thread seeded by replay to fork point, source thread immutability verified, derived forms requeue (AC-3.1 through AC-3.3).

Story 5 (Inference): Complete — ModelCall function over PI model registry, multi-lane routing, provider-error classification (auth/invalid_request terminal, rate_limit/timeout/network retryable, thrown→other), empty_output handling by LHC adapter (AC-4.1 through AC-4.5).

Story 6 (Validation): Complete — all seven assignments validated against PI registry before first derivation use, unreachable lane reporting with kind+(provider,model)+fix, headless-safe reporting (ctx.ui.notify when available, stderr fallback), capture continues on validation failure (AC-5.1 through AC-5.6).

DETERMINED PRODUCTION PATH DEVIATION: Reload for no-flag and --resume uses cwd-most-recent registry selection rather than reconstructing from a prior resolved thread id (EV-001). The implementation acknowledges this as an Epic-1 convenience with concurrent same-cwd limitations.

DETERMINED PRODUCTION PATH DEVIATION: Production --resume presents candidates through ctx.ui.notify but auto-selects most recent thread rather than resolving an explicit operator selection (EV-002). The implementation acknowledges this as a spec deviation due to PI v0.79.2 lacking an interactive input surface.

blockingFindings.title: Reload for no-flag and --resume uses cwd-most-recent registry selection instead of reconstructing from the resolved thread id
blockingFindings.evidence: AC-1.5 requires reload reconstruction from 'the resolved thread id' (epic.md:137). resolveReloadThread for no-flag/--resume uses listed.value.at(-1) after threads.listThreads({cwd}) (thread-resolution.ts:141-145). The code comment (lines 118-121) acknowledges this as an Epic-1 convenience with 'known concurrent same-cwd limitation' and defers precise lineage to Feature 2+. The production test (thread-resolution.test.ts:335-370) only proves the single-thread-in-cwd case. Story 1 verification (014-verify.json) confirms SV-001 is 'needs-human-ruling' with gates passing but production behavior deviating from AC-1.5.

blockingFindings.title: Production --resume auto-selects most recent thread instead of resolving an operator selection
blockingFindings.evidence: AC-1.7 requires --resume to 'resolve the operator's selection' (epic.md:141). defaultSelectThread (index.ts:191-201) presents candidates via ctx.ui.notify but returns mostRecent.threadId without operator input. The code comment (lines 181-190) acknowledges this as 'a precise spec deviation' because PI v0.79.2 'exposes no interactive input/selection surface'. The production test (thread-resolution.test.ts:255-290) asserts notification plus most-recent behavior as the expected path. Story 1 verification (014-verify.json) confirms SV-002 is 'needs-human-ruling' with gates passing but production behavior deviating from AC-1.7.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Documented idempotency edge case for identity-less events
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Story 2 implementation notes SV-001 residual: a truly identity-less event (no entryId AND no source position AND same content) cannot satisfy both stable-on-redelivery AND unique-per-occurrence constraints. Real PI message_end always carries a stable entry id per research, so this edge is unreachable on the production hook path.

nonBlockingFindings.title: PI extension input/selection API unavailable for --resume picker
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Story 1 implementation notes SV-002: PI v0.79.2 exposes no interactive input/selection surface. Production --resume presents candidates via ctx.ui.notify and auto-selects most-recent. Exact operator selection and exact-prior-thread reload are deferred until PI provides the API. This is the root cause of EV-002.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived form reuse optimization deferred for v1
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Story 4 fork implementation always requeues derived forms rather than copying/reusing ready forms. Fork correctness is preserved (AC-3.3 permits reuse 'may'), but provenance-identity safety is not yet implemented. Reuse optimization deferred to Epic 2+.

crossStoryFindings: The implemented epic is mostly coherent across Stories 2-6, and the configured Story/Epic gates pass. The remaining cross-story issue is Story 1 thread identity: reload and resume are foundational to every later capture, fork, verification, and derivation flow, so accepting cwd-most-recent behavior changes the meaning of a recorded thread across the whole epic.
architectureFindings: AC-1.5 says reload reconstructs from durable state, specifically the resolved thread id. The implementation reattaches no-flag and --resume reloads by cwd-most-recent registry row instead of the prior resolved thread id.

AC-1.7 says --resume resolves the operator's selection. The production path presents candidates through ctx.ui.notify, then auto-selects the most recent thread. The tested production behavior matches that deviation, not the literal acceptance criterion.
No context hook is registered for Epic 1, capture/inference/fork/validation modules are wired through real LHC surfaces, and tests exercise temp SQLite threads rather than mocked src modules.

Flows 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 have direct source/tests and latest story-verifier evidence showing pass, including capture gaps, fork replay, model-call routing, startup validation, and replay/inspect verification.
The M0 corpus breadth remains a named spec input; current replay fixtures are synthetic/fixture-backed but the Story 3 implementation drives the real converter and intake path.
productionPathFindings: Material production-path finding: reload for no-flag and --resume uses cwd-most-recent registry selection, which can attach capture to the wrong thread when more than one thread exists for the cwd.
Material production-path finding: production --resume has no real operator selection path; it notifies the list and auto-selects most recent.

No material fake model adapter or fabricated completion path remains in production inference: createModelCall resolves through PI modelRegistry and dynamically imports @earendil-works/pi-ai, returning classified failures if unavailable. Test fakes are confined to test fixtures.

blockingFindings.title: Reload can reattach to the wrong cwd thread
blockingFindings.evidence: Epic AC-1.5 requires reload reconstruction from the resolved thread id (docs/specs/02-pi-lhc/01-connector-core/epic.md:137). resolveReloadThread documents no-flag/--resume reload as cwd-most-recent and returns listed.value.at(-1) (packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts:118, packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts:141). The production test proves only the single-thread cwd case (packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:335). Latest Story 1 verifier also marked this needs-human-ruling in artifacts/01-session-lifecycle-and-thread-resolution/014-verify.json.

blockingFindings.title: Production --resume does not resolve an operator selection
blockingFindings.evidence: Epic AC-1.7 requires --resume to resolve the operator's selection (docs/specs/02-pi-lhc/01-connector-core/epic.md:141). defaultSelectThread states PI lacks an interactive selection surface, notifies candidates, then returns mostRecent.threadId (packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:181, packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:195). The production test asserts the most-recent default as the selected thread (packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:255, packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:289). Latest Story 1 verifier marked this needs-human-ruling in artifacts/01-session-lifecycle-and-thread-resolution/014-verify.json.
